title: Jeremiah Chapter 23 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 23 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 23 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 23.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about the pastors who destroy and scatter the sheep of His pasture?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:1 states, 'Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the LORD.'

questions.question: What will the LORD do to the pastors who have scattered His flock?
options: He will visit upon them the evil of their doings.
questions.correctAnswer: He will visit upon them the evil of their doings.
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 23:2, it says, 'behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the LORD.'

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 23, what will happen to the remnant of the flock?
options: They will be gathered and become fruitful.
questions.correctAnswer: They will be gathered and become fruitful.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:3 states, 'I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries... and they shall be fruitful and increase.'

questions.question: What will the LORD set up over His flock?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:4 mentions, 'And I will set up shepherds over them which shall feed them.'

questions.question: True or False: The King that the LORD will raise unto David will execute judgment and justice.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:5 states that a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice.

questions.question: What name will the King be called according to Jeremiah 23?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:6 states, 'this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.'

questions.question: True or False: The prophets of Jerusalem are described as faithful and righteous.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:14 describes the prophets of Jerusalem as committing adultery and walking in lies.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about those who prophesy lies in His name?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:40 indicates that the LORD will bring an everlasting reproach upon those who prophesy lies.

questions.question: What does the LORD compare His word to in Jeremiah 23?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:29 states, 'Is not my word like as a fire? saith the LORD; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?'

questions.question: True or False: The prophets have been sent by the LORD according to Jeremiah 23.
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 23:21, it says, 'I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran.'

questions.question: In Jeremiah 23, what will happen to those who say, 'The burden of the LORD'?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:34 states, 'I will even punish that man and his house.'

questions.question: What emotion does Jeremiah express because of the prophets in verse 9?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:9 describes his heart as broken because of the prophets.

questions.question: What does the LORD ask about hiding from Him in Jeremiah 23?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:23 asks, 'Am I a God at hand, saith the LORD, and not a God afar off?' indicating it's impossible to hide from Him.

questions.question: True or False: The pleasant places of the wilderness are flourishing according to Jeremiah 23.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:10 states that 'the pleasant places of the wilderness are dried up.'

questions.question: In what order does the LORD address the actions of the prophets and priests in Jeremiah 23?
options: He first punishes them, then forgives them.
He first warns them, then gathers His flock.
He first expresses grief, then condemns them.
He first gathers His flock, then punishes them.
questions.correctAnswer: He first expresses grief, then condemns them.
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with Jeremiah expressing grief over the prophets before detailing their condemnation.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 23 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 23 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will God do to the prophets of Jerusalem who have committed wickedness?
questions.explanation: God declares that He will feed the prophets with wormwood and make them drink the water of gall due to their profaneness. This is stated in Jeremiah 23:15.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 23:16, what effect do the false prophets have on the people?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the false prophets make the people vain by speaking visions of their own hearts rather than from the mouth of the LORD, as indicated in Jeremiah 23:16.

questions.question: What do the false prophets falsely proclaim according to Jeremiah 23:17?
questions.explanation: The false prophets say to those who despise the Lord that they shall have peace, misleading the people, as stated in Jeremiah 23:17.

questions.question: What does the LORD say will happen to the wicked in Jeremiah 23:19?
options: They will experience a whirlwind of fury
questions.correctAnswer: They will experience a whirlwind of fury
questions.explanation: This verse indicates that a grievous whirlwind of the LORD will fall upon the head of the wicked, as stated in Jeremiah 23:19.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 23:22 imply will happen if the prophets had listened to God's counsel?
options: They would have turned the people from evil
questions.correctAnswer: They would have turned the people from evil
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that had the prophets stood in God's counsel, they would have successfully turned the people away from their evil ways, as shown in Jeremiah 23:22.

questions.question: Is God a God who is far off according to Jeremiah 23:23?
options: He is only in the heavens
questions.explanation: God emphasizes that He is indeed a God at hand and not afar off, which conveys His nearness to His people, as stated in Jeremiah 23:23.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 23:24, can anyone hide from God?
options: No, He fills heaven and earth
questions.correctAnswer: No, He fills heaven and earth
questions.explanation: The verse states that no one can hide from God because He fills both heaven and earth, indicating His omnipresence, as shown in Jeremiah 23:24.

questions.question: What do the prophets claim in Jeremiah 23:25?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that the prophets say 'I have dreamed, I have dreamed', which indicates their false claims, as seen in Jeremiah 23:25.

questions.question: True or False: The prophets in Jeremiah 23 are described as speaking the words of God.
questions.explanation: The prophets are criticized for prophesying lies and not speaking God's words, as stated in Jeremiah 23:21.

questions.question: True or False: The word of God is compared to fire and a hammer in Jeremiah 23:29.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:29 compares the word of God to fire and a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces, illustrating its power.

questions.question: What should one say if they inquire about the burden of the LORD according to Jeremiah 23:36?
options: Mention the burden of the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse instructs that one should respond with 'What burden?' indicating that they should not acknowledge the false claims of burden among the people, as shown in Jeremiah 23:36.

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned for the prophet, priest, or people who claim 'The burden of the LORD' in Jeremiah 23:34?
questions.explanation: The verse states that those who claim 'The burden of the LORD' will face punishment, showing God's seriousness about false declarations, as indicated in Jeremiah 23:34.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 23 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 23.

questions.question: What will the LORD do to the prophets who scatter His flock according to Jeremiah 23?
options: He will visit upon them the evil of their doings
questions.correctAnswer: He will visit upon them the evil of their doings
questions.explanation: The LORD states that He will visit upon the pastors the evil of their doings due to their actions of scattering the flock (Jeremiah 23:2).

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to do with the remnant of His flock?
options: He will gather them and bring them to their folds
questions.correctAnswer: He will gather them and bring them to their folds
questions.explanation: The LORD promises to gather the remnant of His flock from all countries and bring them back to their folds (Jeremiah 23:3).

questions.question: What name will the righteous Branch be called according to Jeremiah 23:6?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 23:6, the righteous Branch is named THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 23:10, what is the state of the land?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:10 states that the land is full of adulterers, indicating moral corruption.

questions.question: What will be the fate of the prophets who prophesy falsely according to Jeremiah 23:32?
options: They shall not profit this people at all
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not profit this people at all
questions.explanation: The LORD declares in Jeremiah 23:32 that the false prophets will not profit the people at all.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD encourages His people to listen to the words of the false prophets.
questions.explanation: The LORD explicitly tells the people not to listen to the false prophets who speak visions of their own hearts (Jeremiah 23:16).

questions.question: What literary device is evident in Jeremiah 23:29 where the LORD compares His word to fire?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 23:29, the comparison of God's word to fire is a metaphor illustrating its power and purifying nature.

questions.question: Who is said to have prophesied in Baal, leading Israel to err according to Jeremiah 23:13?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:13 indicates that the prophets of Samaria prophesied in Baal and caused Israel to err.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 23:39, what will happen to those who claim 'the burden of the LORD'?
questions.explanation: The LORD states in Jeremiah 23:34 that those who claim 'the burden of the LORD' will be punished.

questions.question: True or False: The prophets mentioned in Jeremiah Chapter 23 were sent by the LORD.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:21 makes it clear that the LORD did not send the prophets who prophesied falsely.

questions.question: In which New Testament passage is the theme of false prophets echoed, similar to Jeremiah 23?
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:15 warns about false prophets, paralleling the warnings given in Jeremiah 23 regarding deceptive leaders.

questions.question: Which verse emphasizes that God's presence is not limited to a distance according to Jeremiah 23?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 23:24, the LORD emphasizes that He fills heaven and earth, indicating His omnipresence.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word for 'word' in Jeremiah 23:29 signifies the power of God's message?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Dabar' in Jeremiah 23:29 means 'word' and signifies the powerful and authoritative nature of God's message.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 23 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 23 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about the pastors who destroy and scatter His sheep?
questions.explanation: The LORD pronounces a woe upon pastors who destroy and scatter His sheep, emphasizing their wrongdoing. This is stated in Jeremiah 23:1.

questions.question: What will the LORD do to the pastors who have not visited His flock?
options: He will visit upon them the evil of their doings
questions.correctAnswer: He will visit upon them the evil of their doings
questions.explanation: The LORD declares that He will visit upon the pastors the consequences of their evil actions, as highlighted in Jeremiah 23:2.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to do with the remnant of His flock?
options: Gather them out of all countries
questions.correctAnswer: Gather them out of all countries
questions.explanation: The LORD promises to gather the remnant of His flock from all countries where they have been driven, as stated in Jeremiah 23:3.

questions.question: What will the shepherds set up by the LORD provide for His people?
questions.explanation: The shepherds set up by the LORD will feed His people, ensuring they shall fear no more or be dismayed, as expressed in Jeremiah 23:4.

questions.question: How will the days come according to the LORD in reference to David?
questions.explanation: The LORD indicates that He will raise a righteous Branch unto David who will prosper and execute judgment, as mentioned in Jeremiah 23:5.

questions.question: What is the name by which the future king shall be called?
questions.explanation: The future king is named 'THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS' in Jeremiah 23:6, indicating His divine authority and righteousness.

questions.question: What does the LORD say will no longer be spoken about in the latter days?
options: The LORD liveth, which brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD liveth, which brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt
questions.explanation: In the latter days, it will no longer be said that the LORD lives who brought Israel out of Egypt, as stated in Jeremiah 23:7.

questions.question: What is the consequence for the prophets who prophesy lies in the name of the LORD?
questions.explanation: The LORD declares that He will punish those who prophesy lies in His name, as indicated in Jeremiah 23:32, showing His disapproval of false prophecy.

questions.question: What does the LORD compare His word to in Jeremiah 23:29?
questions.explanation: The LORD compares His word to a fire and a hammer that breaks rocks, indicating its power and effectiveness as stated in Jeremiah 23:29.

questions.question: What is the burden of the LORD according to Jeremiah 23:33?
questions.explanation: The LORD instructs that when asked about the burden of the LORD, the response should be that there is no burden, indicating a shift in His message, as cited in Jeremiah 23:33.

questions.question: What will happen to those who continue to say, 'The burden of the LORD'?
questions.explanation: The LORD states that those who continue to claim 'The burden of the LORD' will face punishment, as mentioned in Jeremiah 23:34.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 23:14 reveal about the prophets of Jerusalem?
options: They commit adultery and walk in lies
They lead the people to prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: They commit adultery and walk in lies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:14 clearly states that the prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery and walk in lies, indicating their moral corruption and falsehood.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about the secret places where people think they can hide?
options: The LORD fills heaven and earth
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD fills heaven and earth
questions.explanation: The LORD emphasizes that He fills heaven and earth, underscoring that no one can hide from Him, as stated in Jeremiah 23:24.

questions.question: How does the chapter portray the consequences of false prophecy?
questions.explanation: The chapter illustrates that false prophecies lead people to err and ultimately face destruction, as highlighted in Jeremiah 23:32.

questions.question: What insight do verses 5-6 and verse 11 provide about the nature of God's plans for His people?
options: They include righteous leadership and salvation
They are conditional on human action
questions.correctAnswer: They include righteous leadership and salvation
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 emphasize the promise of a righteous king and salvation for Judah, while verse 11 highlights the wickedness among leaders, indicating that God’s plans are rooted in righteous leadership and the salvation of His people.
